about: The Gospel of the formulary “Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, after the days of the purification of Mary were fulfilled, according to the law of Moses, they took Jesus to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord, as it is written in the law of the Lord: Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord; and to offer a sacrifice, as it is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young doves. And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, and this man was just and God-fearing, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was in him. And he had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord. And in the Spirit he came into the temple. And when His parents were bringing in the child Jesus, in order to do for Him according to the custom of the law, he took Him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said: Now You let Your servant depart, Lord, according to Your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen Your salvation, which You have prepared before the face of all peoples: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and the glory of Your people Israel.

a.g: the days of Mary’s purification were fulfilled
shall be called holy to the Lord
His parents were bringing in the Child Jesus

ex.w039: The preposition introduces the content of a relative clause: “according to what was said”. Its accusative government belongs to an understood antecedent, not to the subject inside the relative clause.
ex.w040: Quod is the subject of “what was said”. Its nominative case reflects its role inside that clause, not the government of the preceding preposition.
